subject: Clarifying default retention windows, residency, and deletion SLAs for requests & outputs
messages:
From: Lucas Ng <lucas@acme-analytics.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>
Cc: sec-questions@acme-analytics.com
Date: Thu, 2 Aug 2028 09:15:00 -0400
Subject: Default retention for request/response data and embeddings — quick clarifying questions

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for the demo yesterday. A couple of follow-ups from our security & infra team about Redwood's default behavior:

1) By default, how long are raw requests and model responses (full tokens) retained in hosted accounts? How does that differ for Dedicated / Private deployments?
2) Are prompts and derivations (e.g., model-generated structured outputs) treated the same as user-provided prompts for retention purposes?
3) We use EU regions — does default retention respect data residency for logs and embeddings (i.e., stored only in EU unless we opt-in)?
4) If we request deletion (via support or an API flag), what is the SLA for complete removal from primary store, cache, backups, and snapshots? Any exceptions (legal hold, audit snapshots)?

Appreciate a concise runbook or steps we can hand to our audit team.

Best,
Lucas
Director, Security — Acme Analytics

---

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>
To: Lucas Ng <lucas@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: sec-questions@acme-analytics.com, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 2 Aug 2028 12:02:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Default retention for request/response data and embeddings — quick clarifying questions

Hi Lucas — thanks for the clear list. High-level answers below; I'll attach the short runbook and loop in Aditya for low-level details around caches and backups.

1) Default retention (hosted API):
   - By default, request/response pairs (raw payloads and returned tokens) are retained for 45 days for hosted accounts. This includes both prompt text and complete model outputs unless the customer enables the opt-out header or a workspace setting.
   - Dedicated: retention is configurable by contract — defaults are typically set to 90 days but can be reduced to a customer-defined TTL during onboarding.
   - Private (VPC / on-prem): Redwood's control plane retains minimal operational metadata only; customer can control data lifecycle entirely. We ship a deletion script for on-prem that purges runtime artifacts.

2) Prompts vs. model-derived outputs:
   - Our classification: user-submitted text (prompts) and model-generated outputs are considered stored artifacts by default. For policy purposes we treat them similarly for retention/exports.
   - However, derivative artifacts (e.g., embeddings, reranked scores, intermediate traces) are on a per-artifact policy: embeddings are persisted separately and follow the embeddings TTL (45 days default) unless explicitly configured.

3) Data residency:
   - For hosted accounts, data is stored in the region you select at workspace creation. Logs, requests/responses, and embeddings are kept within that region by default (EU region stores in EU zones). Cross-region backups are NOT performed unless you enable multi-region replication.

4) Deletion SLA & exceptions:
   - Standard deletion request (hosted via support or API): primary-store deletion completes within 24 hours; caches and KV prefixes are invalidated within 1–3 hours.
   - Background purge (removal from hot/warm stores and indexable logs): completes within 7 days for typical accounts.
   - Backups & cold snapshots: retained according to backup schedule. Our default snapshot retention is 90 days; deletion from snapshot copies follows a best-effort schedule and can take up to 30 days to fully propagate.
   - Exceptions: legal hold, active audit requests, or live incident investigations can delay absolute deletion. We require export/hold flags from the customer to pause purge.

Attachments: a short FAQ and the customer-facing deletion runbook (PDF + Markdown).

I'll let Aditya add a short note about KV/embeddings and whether deletion triggers a re-quantization sweep.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Director, Security & Compliance — Redwood Inference

From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>, Lucas Ng <lucas@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, sec-questions@acme-analytics.com
Date: Fri, 3 Aug 2028 10:23:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Default retention for request/response data and embeddings — quick clarifying questions

Adding the implementation-level details Lucas asked for:

- Embeddings: these live in a vector index service. A deletion request marks associated vectors as tombstones immediately; vector search will exclude them within minutes after tombstoning plus an index refresh (usually 15–60 minutes depending on the index shard). The physical removal from disk happens during the next compaction job (24–72 hours).

- Caches (KV cache / prefix cache): caches are ephemeral and invalidation happens synchronously when deletion is requested. That prevents future requests from hitting stale cached context. However, existing in-flight inference sessions might have KV cache slices held in-memory on GPUs for a short window (seconds–minutes).

- Quantized artifacts & model shards: when we apply deletion to stored token logs, we do not modify deployed model binaries. If a customer requests deletion of request/response logs used for offline analytics (e.g., prompt corpora), we ensure those datasets are dropped from analytics clusters within the purge window.

- Backups & snapshots: our backups are incremental. Deleting a file in the primary store does not immediately remove it from prior snapshot layers; we coordinate snapshot garbage collection and mark the earlier blobs for eventual reclamation. For customers with strict requirements, we offer an accelerated purge option under enterprise agreements (contract addendum) that includes an audit timeline and confirmation.

- API opt-outs & headers: customers can opt-out of storage for specific requests by setting X-Redwood-No-Store: true (accepted for stateless endpoints). This is immediate and prevents request/response from being persisted except for minimal telemetry needed for billing/fraud protection. Opt-out does not apply retroactively to previously stored items.

If helpful I can run a short demo showing tombstone propagation in a staged EU workspace.

- Aditya
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Default retention for request/response data and embeddings — quick clarifying questions

Lucas — thanks for the questions and Kim / Aditya for the detailed replies. Quick customer-facing summary and next steps for your audit pack: 

Summary (one-pager):
- Hosted default: 45-day retention for requests/responses and embeddings; Dedicated & Private are configurable by contract.
- Residency: data remains in the selected region by default; no cross-region replication unless explicitly enabled.
- Deletion flow: immediate tombstone + cache invalidation (minutes) → primary-store purge (24 hours) → index/analytics purge (up to 7 days) → snapshot/backups reclamation (up to 30 days). Exceptions include legal hold and live investigations.

Action items:
1) Kimberly: provide the SOC2-Data-Retention-FAQ.pdf (attached) and the deletion_runbook_v1.md to Lucas' audit contact.
2) Lucas: confirm whether you'd like us to enable the X-Redwood-No-Store header for your sandbox test workspace; we can do a short technical session to validate tombstone-to-visibility timeline.
3) Marissa: follow up with Sales/Legal for accelerated purge addendum pricing if Acme needs guaranteed snapshot deletion within 7 days.

Hope this helps — happy to jump on a quick call next week to walk the auditors through the runbook.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Customer Solutions — Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: SOC2-Data-Retention-FAQ.pdf (customer friendly), deletion_runbook_v1.md (step-by-step delete procedure and support playbook).
